title: Are millionaires really leaving Massachusetts? We don’t know yet.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: IRS data necessary to track Massachusetts millionaire migration post-2023 tax implementation remains unavailable, fueling debates about potential resident exodus.
Massachusetts' population saw a net domestic outflow of more than 30,000 in 2025, but income demographics remain unclear.
The new millionaire tax has raised substantially more revenue than anticipated, but its impact on millionaire migration is undetermined.

title: 7 things to do during a rainy day on the Cape
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Visit the Chatham Shark Center to learn about sharks and participate in family-friendly activities.
Spend a rainy day at Fins Up! Waterpark in Hyannis, with slides, a lazy river, and children's areas.
Explore museums like the John F. Kennedy Hyannis Museum or visit historic homes like Hoxie House in Sandwich.

title: Visit to Boston made Boca Raton resident feel miserable about living in Boca Raton
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Ian Pinto, a 20-year-old from Boca Raton, praised Boston after a four-day visit, calling his hometown inferior.
Pinto highlighted Boston's walkability, public transportation, and affordability compared to Boca Raton's car dependency and high prices.
He expressed admiration for the city's welcoming atmosphere and plans to travel more, inspired to eventually move to Boston.

title: Motorcyclist killed in crash with pickup truck in Raynham
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 31-year-old motorcyclist, Jason Marshall from Taunton, died in a crash with a pickup truck in Raynham Tuesday.
The collision occurred at Route 138 and Elm Street, involving Marshall's 1999 Suzuki TL 1000 and a 2015 Chevy Silverado.
The truck's 57-year-old driver stayed on scene; the accident is under investigation by State Police and Raynham police.

title: N.H. police seek to identify suspects who fatally shot dog in attempted armed robbery
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A dog was shot and killed during an attempted armed robbery in Hollis, New Hampshire, on Tuesday morning.
The robbery involved a man and woman who displayed a firearm and demanded money from the victim.
Police urge residents with security cameras to check footage from 2-4 a.m. to assist in identifying the suspects.

title: Former Red Sox infielder criticized front office: ‘Some people watch the game, some people go on the computer’
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Vaughn Grissom, former Red Sox infielder, criticized Boston's reliance on data over player observation during his tenure.
Grissom was traded to the Angels after hitting .190 in 31 games with the Red Sox, now batting .254 with them.
Red Sox's analytics-heavy approach under Craig Breslow has faced criticism for overshadowing scouting assessments.

title: Authorities investigating 4 family members shot in N.H. as potential attempted murders and suicide
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 29-year-old man died by suicide, and three family members were hospitalized after a shooting in Whitefield, New Hampshire.
New Hampshire Attorney General's office is investigating the shootings as potential attempted murders and suicide.
53-year-old Eric Blake Sr. drove himself to a hospital and remains in stable condition after reporting the incident.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with her psychiatric treatment in the spotlight
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy broke down during her daughter's autopsy testimony, leading to a courtroom recess ordered by Judge Sullivan.
Medical examiner testified Clancy children had injuries consistent with lack of oxygen, indicating possible asphyxiation.
Mental health counselor Latiesha Dukes testified Clancy had frequent passive suicidal thoughts but showed signs of improvement.

title: Acton teen charged with murder used ChatGPT for ‘fantasies’ about killing family, DA says
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Arjun Aravind, 17, was charged with murdering his mother and brother in their Acton home on Tuesday before being arrested Wednesday.
Aravind used ChatGPT to create stories about killing his family, indicating concerning behavior prior to the incident.
Aravind was arraigned on vehicle charges; murder and assault charges will be addressed in Concord District Court.

title: Q&A: Boston’s nightlife czar says the city is just getting started
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Corean Reynolds aims to boost Boston's nightlife by extending business hours and establishing social districts.
Boston's successful summer events led to increased revenue and positive impacts for local businesses.
Plans include improving public transport for nighttime workers and supporting diverse nightlife venues.
